title: Stability-first autoscale controller with cost safeguards
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated fleets require predictable throughput guarantees with minimal oscillation in capacity. Existing reactive autoscalers either oscillate under spiky traffic or scale conservatively and waste reserved GPU hours. Goal: Implement a stability-first controller that satisfies throughput SLOs while enforcing explicit cost-safeguard policies and predictable upper/lower capacity fences.

Scope:
- Define composable target metrics (p50/p95 latency, serving tokens/sec, queue depth, per-tenant throughput budget) and a primary setpoint calculator that prefers latency stability over aggressive throughput chasing.
- Implement scaling algorithms: a slower-acting integral controller with quantile-setpoint smoothing, a surge path for controlled burst absorption (bounded by credit pool), and a short-circuit conservative scaler for emergency capacity shedding.
- Safety limits: per-fleet absolute min/max replicas, gradient clamps (max delta per minute), headroom credit accounting, and a cost-rate throttle that reduces scale-up if projected hourly spend exceeds committed budget thresholds.
- Operator controls: config snippets for policy composition, simulated dry-run mode, and observability surfaces (why-did-i-scale events, debug traces).

Non-goals: deep ML forecasting (we'll integrate a separate forecasting service later), model-variant selection, or tenant-level billing changes in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a policy schema supporting at least three target metrics and a selectable scaling algorithm: stable-integral, surge-burst, emergency-shed
Simulated workload tests show <2% overshoot above throughput SLO for 95% of 30-minute test windows across synthetic spike patterns
Gradient clamps prevent more than 20% capacity change in any 5-minute window unless emergency-shed is triggered
Headroom credit system enforces burst budget and prevents scale-up when credit pool is exhausted; documented behavior in console
Cost-rate throttle blocks scale-ups that would breach configured hourly spend thresholds and emits an actionable alert
End-to-end e2e tests in CI with a small dedicated fleet prove controller maintains latency p95 under configured setpoint while respecting min/max replica bounds
Design doc and operator runbook reviewed and approved by SRE and Product (comments addressed)
